x: ITDA and TADP seek to improve agricultural output through modern inputs, horticulture and fruit plantations and to strengthen tribal livelihoods.

s: What is the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA)?
o: A NABARD body for district rural credit
The district organ implementing MoRD anti-poverty programmes
A statutory body under the Panchayati Raj Act
The agency for tribal farm output in scheduled areas
x: DRDA is the district-level agency that implements the anti-poverty programmes of the Ministry of Rural Development.

s: In which year was CAPART set up under the Ministry of Rural Development?
x: CAPART was set up on 1 September 1986 in New Delhi under MoRD.

s: Which Ministry administers the Vibrant Villages Programme, announced in the Budget 2022-23?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
x: The Vibrant Villages Programme was announced in Budget 2022–23 under the Ministry of Home Affairs and targets villages on the northern border.

s: When did the Balwantrai Mehta Committee, which reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service, submit its report?
x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service and submitted its report in November 1957.

s: In which year was the Drought-Prone Area Programme (DPAP) launched?
x: DPAP dates to 1973-74; the Desert Development Programme (1977-78) covers both hot and cold deserts.

s:
Consider the following statements about rural development programmes:
1. The Community Development Programme (1952) came before Food for Work (1977-78).
2. SGSY was launched in 1999.
3. Bharat Nirman was launched before SGSY.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: CDP (1952) preceded Food for Work (1977-78) and SGSY began in 1999; Bharat Nirman came later, in 2005, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Who originated the Etawah Pilot Project, the first rural-development pilot project, in September 1948?
x: Lt. Col. Albert Mayer, an American town planner, started the Etawah Pilot Project in September 1948, India's first rural-development pilot.

s: 'Garibi Hatao' was first introduced in which Five Year Plan?
x: Garibi Hatao entered planning with the Fifth Plan.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: IRDP went nationwide on 2 October 1980; NES began in 1953, Food for Work in 1977–78 and IRDP experimentally in 1978–79.

s:
Consider the following statements about early rural employment programmes:
1. The Employment Guarantee Scheme first started in Maharashtra in 1972.
2. Antyodaya first started in Rajasthan in 1977-78.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the Employment Guarantee Scheme began in Maharashtra in 1972 and Antyodaya in Rajasthan in 1977-78.

s: During which Plan was the Minimum Needs Programme launched in 1974?
x: The Minimum Needs Programme began in 1974 under the Fifth Plan.

s: When was TRYSEM launched?
x: TRYSEM began on 15 August 1979; IRDP went nationwide on 2 October 1980.

s:
Arrange the following rural development programmes in chronological order:
1. Minimum Needs Programme
2. National Extension Service
3. Bharat Nirman
4. Desert Development Programme
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: NES 1953, Minimum Needs Programme 1974, Desert Development Programme 1977-78, Bharat Nirman 2005.

s: What did the Balwantrai Mehta Committee (1957) recommend after reviewing the CDP and NES?
x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee (report November 1957) suggested democratic decentralisation, which led to Panchayati Raj.

s: Which committee, set up to review the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service, suggested democratic decentralisation?
x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee reviewed CDP and NES and recommended democratic decentralisation in 1957.

s: Which areas does the Desert Development Programme (1977-78) cover?
o: Both hot and cold desert areas
x: DDP covers both hot and cold desert areas.

s: Which was the first rural development programme of India, launched in 1952?
x: The Community Development Programme of 1952 was India's first rural development programme.

s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: PMGSY — 25 December 2000 — Ministry of Rural Development
Jal Jeevan Mission — 15 August 2019 — Ministry of Rural Development
Vibrant Villages Programme — 2022–23 — Ministry of Rural Development
x: PMGSY was launched on 25 December 2000 under the Ministry of Rural Development. PMAY-G is under Rural Development, Jal Jeevan Mission under Jal Shakti, and the Vibrant Villages Programme under Home Affairs.

s: What was the main focus of PMGSY-II, launched in 2013?
o: Through routes and major rural links
x: PMGSY-I (2000) gave new connectivity, PMGSY-II (2013) focused on upgradation and PMGSY-III (2019) on through routes and major rural links.

s: Under PMGSY, what population makes habitations in LWE-affected blocks eligible?
x: The PMGSY norm for LWE-affected blocks is 100+, against 250+ for hill/NE/desert/Schedule V areas and 500+ for plains.

s: Which of the following PMGSY phase – focus pairs is correctly matched?
o: PMGSY-III (2019) – Through routes and major rural links
x: PMGSY-I built new roads, PMGSY-II upgraded them and PMGSY-III covers through routes and major rural links.

s: When was the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana launched?
x: PMGSY was launched on 25 December 2000 under the Ministry of Rural Development.

s: Under PMGSY, habitations of what population in hill States, the North-East, deserts and tribal areas are eligible for connectivity?
x: PMGSY norms are 500+ in plains, 250+ in hill/NE/desert/tribal areas and 100+ in LWE blocks.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: Replacing all Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies
x: The mission aims to stimulate local economic development, enhance basic services and create well-planned clusters. It does not replace Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: A successor and expansion of the PURA approach
A special programme for urban slum redevelopment
A scheme exclusively for tribal hostels
A replacement for the National Extension Service
x: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, launched in 2016, is the successor and expansion of the PURA approach.

s: What population does a Rurban cluster of contiguous villages in a plain or coastal area normally have?
x: For plain and coastal areas, a Rurban cluster comprises contiguous villages with a population of 25,000 to 50,000.

s: Critical Gap Funding under the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is up to what share of project cost?
x: The mission relies mainly on convergence of schemes, with Critical Gap Funding up to 30% of project cost.

s: What does rurbanisation through SPMRM or PURA primarily seek to do?
o: Address the rural-urban divide and distress migration
Widen the rural-urban divide through separate infrastructure systems
Replace all rural occupations with urban occupations
x: Rurbanisation is intended to bridge the rural-urban divide and reduce distress migration by bringing urban amenities and opportunities to rural areas.

s: Under SPMRM, what is the Centre:State funding share for States other than NE and Himalayan States?
x: SPMRM sharing is 60:40, and 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States.

s: Where was the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission launched?
x: SPMRM was launched on 21 February 2016 at Kurubhat in Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh.

s: Who co-authored 'Target 3 Billion', which elaborated the PURA concept, with Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
x: Target 3 Billion, on PURA, was written by Kalam with Srijan Pal Singh.

s: How many Rurban clusters does the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission aim to develop?
x: SPMRM (21 February 2016) aims at 300+ Rurban clusters.

s: Which mission aims at developing villages with 'a rural soul and urban amenities'?
x: SPMRM's Rurban clusters are meant to keep a 'rural soul with urban amenities' and curb distress migration.

s: In which year did Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam explain the PURA concept, on the eve of the 54th Republic Day?
x: Kalam explained PURA on the eve of the 54th Republic Day, in 2003.

s: How many Andhra Pradesh panchayats did the Ministry of Rural Development classify under Rurban clusters in March 2026?
x: In March 2026 MoRD classified 359 AP panchayats under Rurban clusters.

s: Which programme was launched in November 2004 in the 150 most backward districts of India?
x: The National Food for Work Programme began in 2004 in 150 most backward districts; it was later merged into NREGA.

s: The National Rural Drinking Water Programme (2009) was renamed from which earlier programme?
x: ARWSP (1972-73) was renamed NRDWP on 1 April 2009 and was part of Bharat Nirman.

s: How many components did Bharat Nirman (December 2005) have?
x: Bharat Nirman had six components: irrigation, drinking water, electrification, roads, housing and rural telephony.

s: What is the full name of the Saubhagya scheme (2017)?
o: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana
Pradhan Mantri Saral Bijli Gram Yojana
x: Saubhagya is the Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana of the Ministry of Power.

s: Which department became a separate Ministry in 2011 and, since June 2019, has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti?
x: Drinking Water and Sanitation became a separate Ministry in 2011 and has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti since June 2019.

s: What is the objective of ODF Plus under SBM-Gramin Phase II?
o: Provide only individual household toilets in urban areas
Provide pucca houses in difficult terrain
Sustain open-defecation-free status and undertake solid and liquid waste management
x: SBM-Gramin Phase II focuses on sustaining ODF status and managing solid and liquid waste, together described as ODF Plus.

s: What period does the 10-Year Rural Sanitation Strategy of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation cover?
x: The 10-Year Rural Sanitation Strategy (2019-2029) was released by DDWS, Jal Shakti, on 27 September 2019.

s: The Functional Household Tap Connection target under the Jal Jeevan Mission covers which of the following?
o: Rural households and specified public institutions
Only urban households and panchayat offices
x: The target covers every rural household as well as schools, anganwadis, Gram Panchayat buildings, health centres and ashramshalas.

s: What is the prescribed service level under the Jal Jeevan Mission?
